## Generalized attack patterns & preconditions

### SI-object_access_authz

**Object-level authorization missing on per-user records.** Records are fetched by a client-supplied identifier without checking that the record belongs to the caller.
Suggested test: As one synthetic user, request a record owned by another synthetic user by its identifier; expect a denial, not the record.

applicability: idor, bola
- preconditions: authenticated session; guessable or enumerable record identifiers
- invariant: A caller can only read records they own.
- id: SI-object_access_authz · version: 2 · status: active · source_class: swarm-simulation · evidence_level: verified · confidence: high · sources: 2 · last_validation: 2026-10-11 · expiry: 2027-01-09

### SI-server_side_fetch

**Server-side fetch of user-supplied URLs.** The server fetches a user-supplied callback URL without restricting the destination.
Suggested test: Register a callback whose synthetic URL points at an internal-shaped host; expect refusal.

applicability: ssrf
- preconditions: a feature that registers or tests user-supplied webhooks or callbacks
- invariant: Server-side requests only reach allowlisted external destinations.
- id: SI-server_side_fetch · version: 2 · status: active · source_class: swarm-simulation · evidence_level: verified · confidence: medium · sources: 1 · last_validation: 2026-10-11 · expiry: 2027-01-09

### SI-query_injection

**User input interpreted as query syntax.** Search or filter input is concatenated into a query instead of bound as data.
Suggested test: Submit query-syntax characters in a search-style input; expect them to be treated literally.

applicability: injection
- preconditions: a search or filter input passed to a query engine
- invariant: User input is never interpreted as query syntax.
- id: SI-query_injection · version: 2 · status: active · source_class: swarm-simulation · evidence_level: verified · confidence: medium · sources: 1 · last_validation: 2026-10-11 · expiry: 2027-01-09

### SI-output_encoding

**User markup rendered without encoding.** User-supplied content is rendered back as markup instead of encoded text.
Suggested test: Submit a synthetic markup marker in user content; expect it encoded on output.

applicability: output_encoding
- preconditions: user content shown to other users or in a preview
- invariant: User-supplied markup is always encoded on output.
- id: SI-output_encoding · version: 1 · status: active · source_class: swarm-simulation · evidence_level: reproduced · confidence: low · sources: 1 · last_validation: 2026-10-11 · expiry: 2027-01-09

### SI-reset_token_strength

**Weak password reset token.** Password reset accepts predictable, long-lived or reusable tokens.
Suggested test: Attempt a reset confirmation with a predictable or already-used synthetic token; expect rejection.

applicability: weak_reset_flow
- preconditions: a self-service password reset flow
- invariant: A password reset requires an unguessable, single-use, short-lived token.
- id: SI-reset_token_strength · version: 1 · status: active · source_class: swarm-simulation · evidence_level: reproduced · confidence: low · sources: 1 · last_validation: 2026-10-11 · expiry: 2027-01-09

### SI-auth_rate_limit

**Authentication attempts not throttled.** Repeated failed logins or one-time-code guesses for one account are never slowed or locked.
Suggested test: Send a burst of failed attempts for one synthetic account; expect throttling after a small threshold.

applicability: missing_rate_limit
- preconditions: a login or code-verification step reachable without prior throttling
- invariant: Repeated failed authentication attempts for one account are throttled.
- id: SI-auth_rate_limit · version: 1 · status: active · source_class: swarm-simulation · evidence_level: reproduced · confidence: low · sources: 1 · last_validation: 2026-10-11 · expiry: 2027-01-09

## Reusable synthetic scenarios

- `SI-object_access_authz`: As one synthetic user, request a record owned by another synthetic user by its identifier; expect a denial, not the record.
- `SI-server_side_fetch`: Register a callback whose synthetic URL points at an internal-shaped host; expect refusal.
- `SI-query_injection`: Submit query-syntax characters in a search-style input; expect them to be treated literally.
- `SI-output_encoding`: Submit a synthetic markup marker in user content; expect it encoded on output.
- `SI-reset_token_strength`: Attempt a reset confirmation with a predictable or already-used synthetic token; expect rejection.
- `SI-auth_rate_limit`: Send a burst of failed attempts for one synthetic account; expect throttling after a small threshold.

## Invariants & defensive patterns

- `SI-object_access_authz`: A caller can only read records they own. Defense: Scope every lookup by the caller in the data-access layer, not the UI.
- `SI-server_side_fetch`: Server-side requests only reach allowlisted external destinations. Defense: Resolve and check destinations against an allowlist; block internal ranges.
- `SI-query_injection`: User input is never interpreted as query syntax. Defense: Use parameterized queries or a query builder; never build query strings.
- `SI-output_encoding`: User-supplied markup is always encoded on output. Defense: Encode by output context in the template layer; sanitize allowed markup.
- `SI-reset_token_strength`: A password reset requires an unguessable, single-use, short-lived token. Defense: Use high-entropy single-use tokens with a short expiry, bound to the account.
- `SI-auth_rate_limit`: Repeated failed authentication attempts for one account are throttled. Defense: Throttle per account and per client, with backoff or temporary lockout.

## Verified mitigation & regression guidance

- `SI-object_access_authz`: Scope every lookup by the caller in the data-access layer, not the UI. Regression: Keep a cross-user read test for every per-user record type.
- `SI-server_side_fetch`: Resolve and check destinations against an allowlist; block internal ranges. Regression: Test internal-shaped destinations on every change to callback handling.
- `SI-query_injection`: Use parameterized queries or a query builder; never build query strings. Regression: Keep a literal-handling test for each search and filter input.
